canonicalExplanation.summary: Readable text comes from a few measurable choices: a comfortable **size** (about 1rem or larger for body text), a **line length** (measure) of roughly 45–75 characters (`max-width: 65ch`), a **unitless line-height** around 1.5 so it scales with the text, clear heading sizes, and containers that **grow** instead of clipping when text gets longer — for translations or 200% zoom.

sections.heading: Start here
sections.body:
A blog post stretches edge to edge on a wide monitor: 180 characters per line, 13px text, tight lines. Readers lose their place jumping back to the start of each line. Squeezing more words on screen didn't help — it hurt. Article text uses a bounded measure and unitless line-height, while containers expand for longer translated labels. In this lesson you'll create and audit readable body, heading and code typography at 200 percent zoom.

Smaller isn't better

includes: Set readable body size, measure, unitless line-height and heading scale.
Audit text at 200% zoom and with longer content.

outcomes: Create and audit readable body, heading and code typography at 200 percent zoom.

examples.title: An article that reads comfortably
examples.situation: Article text uses a bounded measure and unitless line-height while containers expand for longer translated labels.
walkthrough: **Bounded measure:** `.article { max-width: 65ch }` keeps lines around 65 characters even on wide screens.
**Unitless line-height:** `line-height: 1.6` scales for body text, headings and zoomed text alike.
**Expanding containers:** buttons have no fixed height, so the German label "Kurs fortsetzen und speichern" wraps and the button grows. The browser will render it cleanly at 200% zoom.
examples.result: The article reads comfortably at any width, and longer translated labels fit without clipping.

examples.title: The fixed-height button
examples.situation: `.btn { height: 40px; }` works in English. In Tamil, the label wraps to two lines and the second line is cut off.
walkthrough: The fixed height can't grow with the text.
At 200% zoom even the English label overflows.
Fix: replace height with padding and `min-height`, so the button grows as needed.
examples.result: Buttons fit their labels in every language and zoom level.

misconceptions.mistakenBelief: Smaller text always fits more content and therefore improves usability.
misconceptions.correction: Small text and long lines make reading slower and harder, especially on small screens and for people with low vision. Readable size, bounded line length, generous line-height and flexible containers improve usability.
misconceptions.diagnosticPrompt: In "An article that reads comfortably", which two measures made lines easy to follow?

analogy.example: Readable typography is like a **well-designed newspaper column**: narrow enough that your eyes find the next line, spaced enough that lines don't blur, and printed large enough to read on a train.
usefulFor: seeing size as usability, not decoration
limitations: Newspapers have fixed page widths; web pages must adapt.
Web text must also survive zoom and translation.

remediation.explanation: Checklist per text style: **size ≥ 1rem for body? line length ≤ ~75ch? unitless line-height? no fixed height on its container? readable at 200% zoom?**

recap.summary: To create and audit readable typography, use a body size of at least 1rem, a bounded measure around 65ch, unitless line-height, a clear heading scale, and containers without fixed heights — then check everything at 200 percent zoom and with longer content.
